calls.head: The Capitals can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Panthers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Capitals’ kill is near the bottom. The Capitals need to stay out of the box. The Panthers draw a lot of penalties, so their power play should get its chances.
calls.call: The Panthers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.4 expected goals per 60.

calls.head: Patience vs. spray-and-pray
calls.body: On shot quality, Washington is one of the league’s best, but Florida is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances are likely to be the Capitals’.

surprises.head: Florida hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Florida is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams, but it hardly showed tonight: a hit score of 104 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 155 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Bennett wins it with 24 seconds left
paras: Cole Hutson got the scoring started for the Capitals on the power play midway through the first. Aaron Ekblad tied it 1-1 for Florida on the power play early in the second. Hutson scored again with just under seven minutes left to put the Capitals back ahead 2-1, but Eetu Luostarinen tied it 2-2 for Florida with a little over four minutes left. Sam Bennett scored his 200th NHL goal with 24 seconds left to put the Panthers ahead for good.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Panthers had five shots in the first period and trailed 1-0, then outshot the Capitals 26-13 the rest of the way. Jacob Markström made 24 saves for the Panthers, and Logan Thompson stopped 28 of 31 at the other end. The Cats moved to 15-8-3 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Capitals fell to 11-12-0, sixth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Panthers.
Ryan Leonard has a point in seven straight games.
The Capitals’ Vincent Desharnais was back in the lineup after missing 13 games.
Jordan Kyrou faces his old team, St. Louis, on Saturday.
